checks.evidence: Brownian W starts at zero, has continuous paths, mean-zero independent Gaussian increments, and Var(W(t)-W(s))=t-s. Independence is correctly qualified as increments over disjoint intervals. The folded theta=theta0+sqrt(2D)W continues to imply variance2Dt with the same convention. No claim that whole recurrent spike trains are independent.

Kronecker delta meaning is correct. dM=dN-rdt is the centered conditional count increment. Under the immediately stated local conditional-Poisson assumptions it has zero mean and variance rate r. F is the conditional mean activation drift -s/tau+phi(g). Independent standard Brownian dB has zero mean and variance dt; sqrt(r)dB matches centered count variance rdt to leading order. Existing weak-fluctuation and leading covariance qualifications remain.

K is the Jacobian -I/tau+diag(phi')W acting on delta s and gives deterministic first-order mean activation-change rate. R=diag(rbar) collects conditionally independent Poisson spike variance rates at the fixed point; R^(1/2)dB therefore has covariance Rdt. Descriptions agree with formulas and do not assert symmetric K.
u is tangent and Ku=0. v^TK=0 together with v^Tu=1 extracts lasting delta theta. Moving purpose before defining equations does not change normalization or decaying-mode argument.

Likelihood now explicitly holds observed counts fixed while varying proposed theta. Definition correctly identifies assigned data probabilities and distinguishes likelihood from a parameter probability distribution. Fold retains original independent-Poisson likelihood, log and score proof.

theta0=x fixes observation origin at cue. eta is transition displacement and epsilon is y-theta observation error; independent zero-mean Gaussian approximation agrees with transition variance2Dh and observation variance1/(Jh). Independence is restricted to this approximation; many-spike/weak-fluctuation and arbitrarily-short-bin cautions remain. Later storage/readout decomposition still states its separate unbiasedness and history conditions.

For D>0,J>0,L>0, P=sqrt(J/(2D))tanh(sqrt(2DJ)L) solves P'=J-2DP^2,P(0)=0. Reciprocal gives exposed V=sqrt(2D/J)coth(sqrt(2DJ)L). coth=(exp(2z)+1)/(exp(2z)-1) is correct, decreases for z>0 and tends to1. Finite result retains existing local Gaussian model scope. Numerically coth(1)=1.3130352855,coth(2)=1.0373147207,coth(3)=1.0049698233 match rounded main-text ratios.

xi is correctly treated as ideal white-noise drive rather than an ordinary variable with finite point variance. The bridge xi_i dt=sqrt(r_i)dB_i states its conditional integrated variance r_i dt and independent increments. This agrees with original Poisson-strength Gaussian approximation and noise placement solely in s block. Subsequent diffusion2D=sum a_i^2 rbar_i and replacement tau+tau_m remain unchanged.

z=L/L*=sqrt(2DJ)L is dimensionless since2DJ has units1/time^2. Dividing ideal V by sqrt(2D/J) gives coth z; dividing naive2DL/3+1/(JL) by same scale gives z/3+1/z. Min at z=sqrt3 and value2/sqrt3 agree.
